# planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction (Resource)

PostgresIPRestriction Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Allow connections to every schema, as any role, from these ranges.
resource "planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction" "office" {
  organization = "my-organization"
  database     = "my-database"

  cidrs       = ["203.0.113.0/24", "198.51.100.7/32"]
  description = "Office network and VPN gateway"
}

# Limit one role to the addresses of the hosts that use it.
resource "planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction" "reporting" {
  organization = "my-organization"
  database     = "my-database"

  role  = "reporting"
  cidrs = [for ip in ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.11"] : "${ip}/32"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cidrs` (List of String) The IPv4 ranges allowed to connect, in CIDR notation, e.g. `["203.0.113.0/24", "198.51.100.7/32"]`. Use `/32` for a single address.
- `database` (String) The name of the database. Requires replacement if changed.
- `organization` (String) The name of the organization the database belongs to. Requires replacement if changed.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description of the entry, at most 255 characters. Set to an empty string to clear it.
- `role` (String) The Postgres role the entry applies to. Leave unset to apply to all roles. Default: ""
- `schema` (String) The Postgres schema the entry applies to. Leave unset to apply to all schemas. Default: ""

### Read-Only

- `actor` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actor))
- `id` (String) The ID of the IP restriction entry

<a id="nestedatt--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actor`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The ID of the actor

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction.my_planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction
  id = jsonencode({
    database     = "..."
    id           = "..."
    organization = "..."
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction.my_planetscale_postgres_ip_restriction '{"database": "...", "id": "...", "organization": "..."}'
```
